7345ad28b6.why: The new lure 'About ninety-nine in every hundred' is a real slip (counting every idea tested, not the passes) and is truly wrong: about 5 false passes beside 1 true one gives 5 in 6 (PPV about 0.17 on Ioannidis's formula). Two choices now say most passes are false, so the player has to do the sum. Jager and Leek's 14 percent in top medical journals is attributed. Voice and grade are fine.

ad5bf17908.why: Power is now named and taught in the stem, and the question asks across many studies, so the old clarity problem is fixed. The key matches Button et al. 2013 (low power lowers the chance that a significant result reflects a true effect; median power 21 percent). The stem's '1 time in 20' is used by a lure, not against one, and two choices say 'lowers'. Q1's card does not settle this one.

c37744e042.why: The dead birth-date lure is replaced by 'That no single study, however careful, can be trusted on its own'. That is truly wrong: the three proposed disclosure rules (six requirements for authors, four guidelines for reviewers), not distrust of every study, and 'however careful' makes it false. 'Significant' is now taught in the stem. The card now says one group was left out (the Hot Potato condition), the 61 percent figure is attributed to their simulations, and the first rule (deciding the stopping rule in advance) is right. The card does not give away Q5 or Q10.

aa518c8884.why: The stem does not hand over the key. It sets the case (he looked at the scores, then tested the older half), and the key's counterfactual ('Different data would have led him to test another group') shares no wording with the stem ('scores', 'older half'). The lure 'leaving out half of his volunteers' borrows the stem's own words instead. The key is Gelman and Loken's own point: a single test based on the data, where different data would have led to a different test. The case is now set apart as 'Suppose a researcher', and the card says 'above 1 in 20, by more the more paths', which fixes the fact-check note. The choices are of balanced length.

5b05dedc9a.why: 'filed away unpublished' is now 'go unpublished', and the name 'file drawer problem' has to stay. Franco, Malhotra and Simonovits: 221 TESS experiments, 2002-2012; nearly 65 percent of null studies never written up; strong results 40 points more likely to be published. The key and all three lures fit the record.

a6eadd086b.why: The choices now split two 'held to a rule' and two 'judged that', so the frame tell is gone. 'repeats need the first author's approval' is not on record and is truly wrong (French: rejected without review 'on the basis that the journal has a policy of not publishing replications'). The stem has dropped its '50 students', so the too-few lure is live. The key is not the longest choice.

437dd15ea7.why: The key 'Young researchers he was supervising' fits the record: three young Tilburg researchers under Stapel's supervision took their doubts to Marcel Zeelenberg (Nature; Wikipedia). 'Statisticians at another university who checked his numbers' is truly false for Stapel; no source has statisticians elsewhere reporting him, and 'at another university' keeps it apart from his own group, who did find the irregularities. The stem no longer rules out a lure, and choices now split two plural and two singular. The card's 'asked to name his schools, Stapel said they did not exist' matches Wikipedia (the rector asked). The Levelt quote and the 55 publications check out.

199196b084.why: The key now says 'Both graphs came from a single set of data', which fixes the fact-check (some curves were made from formulas, never measured). The card says 'one set of data had been used twice' and names the formulas. The lures (one machine, same day, devices alike) are the misconceptions F25 names, and all are wrong. Sohn, McEuen, and the September 2002 Beasley committee check out.

f961edb5f9.why: The stem now names both kinds of paper. Scheel, Schijen and Lakens 2021: 96 percent positive in standard reports against 44 percent in registered reports. The gap held without the direct replications, and the authors' own caveat is in the card. Chambers and Cortex 2013 check out. Defining the format lets a student reason toward the key, but that reasoning is the ninth-grade point, not a word match.
